contents.html: This Recommendation specifies techniques for the derivation of additional keying material from a secret key – either established through a key-establishment scheme or shared through some other manner – using pseudorandom functions: HMAC, CMAC, and KMAC.

contents.html: Introduction
contents.html_ja: はじめに

contents.html: When a party obtains a cryptographic key, additional keys will often be needed. There are numerous methods for obtaining the keying material required by approved cryptographic algorithms (see SP 800-133, Rev. 2 [1] for a discussion of the recommended techniques). The requisite keying material is often obtained from the output of a key-derivation function (KDF) that takes a preexisting cryptographic key (and other data) as input. Key-derivation functions are used to derive additional keys from a cryptographic key.

The key-derivation functions specified in the original edition (2008) of NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-108 used HMAC and CMAC as pseudorandom functions. In Revision 1, a KDF using KMAC is added in Section 4.4.
1 Chen L (2008) Recommendation for Key Derivation Using Pseudorandom Functions. (National Institute of Standards and Technology, Gaithersburg, MD), NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-108.
contents.html_ja: ¹ Chen L（2008）『疑似乱数関数を用いる鍵導出に関する推奨事項』。（米国国立標準技術研究所、メリーランド州ゲイザースバーグ）、NIST特別刊行物（SP）800-108。

contents.html: Scope and Purpose
contents.html_ja: 適用範囲と目的

contents.html: This Recommendation specifies several families of key-derivation functions that use pseudorandom functions. These key-derivation functions can be used to derive additional keys from an existing cryptographic key that was previously established through an automated key-establishment scheme (e.g., as defined in SP 800-56A [2] and SP 800-56B [3]), previously generated (e.g., using a pseudorandom bit generator as specified in SP 800-90A [4] or a previous instance of key derivation as specified in this Recommendation), and/or previously shared in some other way (e.g., by manual distribution). Effectively, the key-derivation functions specified in this Recommendation provide the key expansion functionality described in SP 800-56C [5], where key derivation is portrayed as a process that potentially requires two separate steps: 1) randomness extraction (to obtain an initial key) and 2) key expansion (to produce additional keys from that initial key and other data).
contents.html_ja: 本勧告は、疑似乱数関数を用いる複数の鍵導出関数群を規定する。これらの鍵導出関数は、自動鍵確立方式（例：[2]のSP 800-56Aおよび[3]のSP 800-56Bに規定）によって以前に確立された暗号鍵、既に生成された暗号鍵（例：[4]のSP 800-90Aに規定する疑似乱数ビット生成器を用いて生成したもの、または本勧告に規定する鍵導出を以前に実行して得たもの）、および／またはその他の方法（例：手動配布）で以前に共有された暗号鍵から、追加の鍵を導出するために使用できる。実質的に、本勧告に規定する鍵導出関数は、SP 800-56C [5]で説明される鍵拡張機能を提供する。同文書では、鍵導出は、場合によっては二つの別個の段階、すなわち1) 初期鍵を得るためのランダム性抽出、2) その初期鍵およびその他のデータから追加の鍵を生成する鍵拡張、を必要とする処理として示されている。

contents.html: Pseudorandom Function (PRF)

A pseudorandom function (PRF) is the basic building block for constructing a key-derivation function in this Recommendation. Generally, a PRF family \(\{\mathit{PRF}(s, x) \mid s \in S\}\) consists of polynomial-time computable functions with an index (also called a seed) \(s\) and input \(x\), such that when \(s\) is randomly selected from \(S\) and not known to observers, \(\mathit{PRF}(s, x)\) is computationally indistinguishable from a random function defined on the same domain with output to the same range as \(\mathit{PRF}(s, x)\). For a formal definition of a pseudorandom function, refer to [9]. When a cryptographic key \(K_{\mathit{IN}}\) is regarded as the seed, that is, \(s = K_{\mathit{IN}}\), the output of the pseudorandom function can be used as keying material. In Section 4, several families of PRF-based key-derivation functions are defined without describing the internal structure of the PRF. For key derivation, this Recommendation approves the use of the keyed-Hash Message Authentication Code (HMAC) specified in [7], the Cipher-based Message Authentication Code (CMAC) specified in [6], and the Keccak-based Message Authentication Code (KMAC) specified in [8] as pseudorandom functions. For a given KDF using HMAC, CMAC, or KMAC, the key \(K_{\mathit{IN}}\) is assumed to be computationally indistinguishable from one that has been selected uniformly at random from the set of all the bit strings with a length of \(|K_{\mathit{IN}}|\).
contents.html_ja: 疑似乱数関数（PRF）は、本勧告における鍵導出関数を構成するための基本的な構成要素である。一般に、PRF族 \(\{\mathit{PRF}(s, x) \mid s \in S\}\) は、添字（シードとも呼ばれる）\(s\) と入力 \(x\) を持つ多項式時間で計算可能な関数から成る。\(s\) が \(S\) からランダムに選択され、観測者に知られていない場合、\(\mathit{PRF}(s, x)\) は、同じ定義域上で定義され、\(\mathit{PRF}(s, x)\) と同じ値域に出力するランダム関数と計算量的に識別不能である。疑似乱数関数の形式的な定義については[9]を参照されたい。暗号鍵 \(K_{\mathit{IN}}\) をシードとみなす、すなわち \(s = K_{\mathit{IN}}\) とすると、疑似乱数関数の出力を鍵素材として使用できる。第4節では、PRFに基づく複数の鍵導出関数族を、PRFの内部構造を記述せずに定義する。鍵導出において、本勧告は、[7]に規定する鍵付きハッシュメッセージ認証コード（HMAC）、[6]に規定する暗号方式ベースのメッセージ認証コード（CMAC）、および[8]に規定するKeccakベースのメッセージ認証コード（KMAC）を疑似乱数関数として使用することを承認する。HMAC、CMAC、またはKMACを用いる所与のKDFでは、鍵 \(K_{\mathit{IN}}\) は、長さ \(|K_{\mathit{IN}}|\) のすべてのビット列の集合から一様ランダムに選択された鍵と計算量的に識別不能であると仮定する。

contents.html: When selecting the PRF to be used by a key-derivation function, consider using HMAC or KMAC rather than CMAC, unless, for example, AES is the only primitive implemented in the platform or using CMAC has a resource benefit. When CMAC is used as the PRF, a party with knowledge of the key-derivation key and the freedom to choose a sufficient number of input bits may be able to force one or more derived blocks of keying material to predetermined values. Mitigations are provided to guard against this type of key control in cases where CMAC is used as the PRF when implementing a KDF as specified in this Recommendation (see Sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, and 6.7).

contents.html: Key-Derivation Function (KDF)
contents.html_ja: 鍵導出関数（KDF）

contents.html:
This section defines several families of key-derivation functions (KDFs) that use PRFs. For the purposes of this Recommendation, a KDF is a function that – given input consisting of a (secret) key and other data – is used to generate (i.e., derive) keying material that can be employed by cryptographic algorithms. In other words, the KDFs specified here provide a key-expansion capability (as noted in Section 2).

Depending on the intended length of the keying material to be derived, the KDF may require multiple invocations of the PRF used in its construction. A method for iterating the multiple invocations is called a mode of iteration. In this Recommendation, a counter mode, a feedback mode, and a double-pipeline mode are specified in Sections 4.1, 4.2, and 4.3, respectively, as iteration modes.

In addition to these iteration modes, this Recommendation specifies a KDF using KMAC in Section 4.4. KMAC can output keying material that has the required length without iteration.

The key that is input to a key-derivation function is called a key-derivation key (KDK). To comply with this Recommendation, a KDK shall be a cryptographic key (see Appendix D). The KDK used as an input to one of the key-derivation functions specified in this Recommendation can, for example, be generated by an approved cryptographic random bit generator (e.g., by a deterministic random bit generator of the type specified in [4]) and manually distributed, or it could be obtained from the output of an approved automated key-establishment scheme (e.g., as defined in [2] and [3]). The KDK can be a portion of the keying material derived from another KDK.

contents.html: Note that the key-derivation methods employed as components of key-agreement schemes (as described in [2], [3], and [5]) include two-step methods in which the first step consists of extracting a KDK from a shared secret precursor. These extracted KDKs are not part of the output of a key-agreement scheme. They are only used to derive output keying material during a single execution of a scheme and then destroyed (along with all other sensitive, locally stored data associated with that particular execution).

In keeping with the usual terminology, the output of a key-derivation function is called the derived keying material and may subsequently be segmented into multiple keys. Any disjoint segments of the derived keying material (with the required lengths) can be used as cryptographic keys for the intended algorithms. Two different key-establishment scenarios may use the KDF: one in which multiple parties share the same key-derivation key and are able to separately derive the same keying material, and the other in which one entity derives keying material using a key-derivation key known only to itself and distributes the derived keying material to other entities. When multiple parties share the same key-derivation key, the cryptographic application employing a KDF must define the way to convert (i.e., parse) the keying material into different keys. For example, when 256 bits of keying material are derived, the application may specify that the first 128 bits will be used as a key for a message authentication code and that the second 128 bits will be used as an encryption key for a given encryption algorithm. In the case where a single party derives the keying material, a re-derivation can produce the same keys (when required).
To define key-derivation functions, the following notations are used. Some of the notations have been defined in Appendix C, but definitions are included here for easy reference.

Therefore, KMAC128 or KMAC256 shall be used for the key-derivation function.

contents.html: Key Hierarchy
contents.html_ja: 5. 鍵階層

contents.html: The keying material derived from a given key-derivation key could subsequently be used as one or more key-derivation keys to derive still more key-derivation keys. In this way, a key hierarchy could be established. In a key hierarchy, a KDF is used with a higher-level “parent” key-derivation key (and other appropriate input data) to derive a number of lower-level “child” keys. Fig. 5 presents a three-level key hierarchy as an example. In this example, the second-level key-derivation keys \(K_{\mathit{IN}}^{(1)}\), \(K_{\mathit{IN}}^{(2)}\), \(K_{\mathit{IN}}^{(3)}\), and an additional second-level (non-key-derivation) key, \(K_{\mathit{non\text{-}KDK}}\), are all derived from the top-level key \(K_{\mathit{IN}}\). The keys \(K_{\mathit{IN}}^{(1)}\), \(K_{\mathit{IN}}^{(2)}\), and \(K_{\mathit{IN}}^{(3)}\) are then used to derive the bottom-level keys in this key hierarchy (i.e., \(K_{11}\), \(K_{12}\),..\(K_{32}\)). In any key hierarchy, only designated key-derivation keys are used to derive lower-level keys, and those key-derivation keys shall not be used for any purpose other than key derivation.
contents.html_ja: 所与の鍵導出鍵から導出された鍵素材は、その後、1つ以上の鍵導出鍵として使用し、さらに鍵導出鍵を導出してもよい。このようにして鍵階層を確立できる。鍵階層では、KDFを上位の「親」鍵導出鍵（および適切なその他の入力データ）とともに用い、複数の下位の「子」鍵を導出する。図5に三階層の鍵階層を例として示す。この例では、第2レベルの鍵導出鍵 \(K_{\mathit{IN}}^{(1)}\)、\(K_{\mathit{IN}}^{(2)}\)、\(K_{\mathit{IN}}^{(3)}\) と、追加の第2レベルの（鍵導出用ではない）鍵 \(K_{\mathit{non\text{-}KDK}}\) は、すべて最上位の鍵 \(K_{\mathit{IN}}\) から導出される。続いて、鍵 \(K_{\mathit{IN}}^{(1)}\)、\(K_{\mathit{IN}}^{(2)}\)、\(K_{\mathit{IN}}^{(3)}\) は、この鍵階層の最下位の鍵（すなわち \(K_{11}\)、\(K_{12}\)、..\(K_{32}\)）を導出するために使用される。いかなる鍵階層でも、指定された鍵導出鍵だけを下位の鍵の導出に用い、それらの鍵導出鍵は鍵導出以外の目的に使用してはならない。

contents.html: Security Considerations
contents.html_ja: 6. セキュリティ上の考慮事項

contents.html: An improperly defined key-derivation function can make the derived keying material vulnerable to attacks. This section will discuss some factors that affect the cryptographic strength of the keying material derived by a KDF. However, some of the required security properties cannot be achieved by the key-derivation function itself. For example, the overall security of the derived keying material depends on the protocols that establish the key-derivation key. These external conditions are out of the scope of the security discussion in this Recommendation.
contents.html_ja: 不適切に定義された鍵導出関数を使用すると、導出鍵素材が攻撃に対して脆弱になるおそれがある。本節では、KDFによって導出される鍵素材の暗号学的強度に影響する要因をいくつか説明する。ただし、必要なセキュリティ特性の一部は、鍵導出関数自体では実現できない。例えば、導出鍵素材の全体的なセキュリティは、鍵導出鍵を確立するプロトコルに依存する。こうした外部条件は、本勧告のセキュリティに関する説明の対象外である。

contents.html: Cryptographic Strength
contents.html_ja: 暗号学的強度

contents.html: The security strength of a key-derivation function is measured by the amount of work required to distinguish the output of the KDF from a uniformly distributed bit string of the same length, under the assumption that the key-derivation key, \(K_{\mathit{IN}}\), is the only unknown input to the KDF. This is certainly no greater than the work required to recover \(K_{\mathit{IN}}\) and/or the remaining portions of the derived keying material from a given segment of KDF output. Knowing the data used as input to the KDF (other than the \(w\)-bit key-derivation key \(K_{\mathit{IN}}\)) and observing corresponding output data of sufficient bit length (say, \(w\) bits or more), one can very likely recover the key \(K_{\mathit{IN}}\) through an exhaustive search over its possible values, performing (at most) \(2^w\) executions of the KDF.
contents.html_ja: 鍵導出関数のセキュリティ強度は、鍵導出鍵 \(K_{\mathit{IN}}\) だけがKDFへの未知の入力であるとの前提で、KDFの出力を同じ長さの一様分布ビット列から識別するために必要な作業量によって測定される。これは、KDF出力の所与のセグメントから \(K_{\mathit{IN}}\) および／または導出鍵素材の残りの部分を復元するために必要な作業量を超えないことは確かである。KDFへの入力として用いたデータ（\(w\) ビットの鍵導出鍵 \(K_{\mathit{IN}}\) を除く）を知り、十分なビット長（例えば \(w\) ビット以上）の対応する出力データを観測すれば、鍵 \(K_{\mathit{IN}}\) は、その取り得る値を総当たり探索し、（最大で）\(2^w\) 回のKDF実行を行うことによって、高い確率で復元できる。

contents.html: For a secure KDF, the revelation of one portion of the derived keying material must not degrade the security of any other portion of that keying material. For example, the compromise of some derived keys (or the revelation of derived IVs) must not enhance an adversary’s ability to predict or determine the value of any other (secret) keying material derived during the same execution of the KDF.
contents.html_ja: 安全なKDFでは、導出鍵素材の一部分が明らかになっても、同じ鍵素材の他の部分の安全性が低下してはならない。例えば、導出鍵の一部が侵害された場合（または導出されたIVが明らかになった場合）でも、同じKDF実行で導出された他の（秘密の）鍵素材の値を予測または特定する攻撃者の能力が高まってはならない。

contents.html: The Length of a Key-Derivation Key
contents.html_ja: 鍵導出鍵の長さ

contents.html: It is recommended that the length of a KDK used by a KDF be at least as large as the targeted security strength (in bits) of any application that will be supported by the use of the derived keying material. This may affect the choice of the MAC algorithm used to implement a PRF-based key-derivation function, since the possibilities for the KDK size are determined by what is allowed for the MAC keys. For example, when using CMAC as a PRF, the key length is uniquely determined by the underlying block cipher. In this case, an implementation should check whether the key-derivation key length is consistent with the length required by the PRF. However, some PRFs can accommodate different key lengths. If HMAC is used as the PRF, then a KDF can use a key-derivation key of essentially any length. It is worth noting, however, that if the chosen key is longer than one input block for the hash function underlying HMAC, that key will be hashed, and the (much shorter) \(h\)-bit output will be used as the HMAC key instead. In this case, given a pair consisting of the input data (other than the key) and enough corresponding output of the KDF, the hashed key can likely be recovered in (at most) \(2^h\) computations of the KDF. Therefore, the security strength of an HMAC-based key-derivation function may be decreased by increasing the length of the KDK beyond the length of an input block of the underlying hash function.
contents.html_ja: KDFで用いるKDKの長さは、導出鍵素材を利用するアプリケーションが目標とするセキュリティ強度（ビット単位）以上であることが推奨される。これは、PRFベースの鍵導出関数を実装するMACアルゴリズムの選択に影響することがある。KDKのサイズはMAC鍵に許容されるサイズによって決まるためである。例えば、CMACをPRFとして使用する場合、鍵長は基礎となるブロック暗号によって一意に決まる。この場合、実装では鍵導出鍵の長さがPRFに必要な長さと整合しているかを確認すべきである。ただし、一部のPRFは異なる鍵長に対応できる。HMACをPRFとして用いる場合、KDFでは実質的に任意の長さの鍵導出鍵を使用できる。ただし、選択した鍵がHMACの基礎となるハッシュ関数の1入力ブロックより長い場合、その鍵はハッシュされ、その代わりに（はるかに短い）\(h\) ビットの出力がHMAC鍵として使用されることに注意する価値がある。この場合、入力データ（鍵以外）と十分な対応するKDF出力の組があれば、ハッシュされた鍵は（最大で）\(2^h\) 回のKDF計算で復元できる可能性が高い。したがって、HMACベースの鍵導出関数のセキュリティ強度は、KDKの長さを基礎となるハッシュ関数の入力ブロック長より長くすることで低下することがある。

contents.html: Converting Keying Material to Cryptographic Keys
contents.html_ja: 鍵素材から暗号鍵への変換

contents.html: The length of the derived keying material \(L\) depends on the requirements of the cryptographic algorithms that rely on the KDF output. The length of a given cryptographic key is determined by the algorithm that will employ it (e.g., a block cipher or a message authentication code) and the desired security strength. In the absence of limitations that may be imposed by relying applications, any segment of the derived keying material that has the required length can be specified for use as a key, subject to the following restriction: when multiple keys (or any other types of parameters, such as initialization vectors) are obtained from the derived keying material, they shall be selected from disjointed (i.e., non-overlapping) segments of the KDF output. Therefore, the value of \(L\) shall be greater than or equal to the sum of the lengths of the keys and other types of parameters that will be obtained from the derived keying material. Care must be taken to avoid confusion when parsing KDF output if any segments are used as public parameters (such as public IVs). Attacks on the protocol level may attempt to cause one party to mistakenly release a secret portion of the KDF output. The security of any protocol using the derived keying material is beyond the scope of this Recommendation. The use of the derived keying material as a key stream (as in a stream cipher) is not recommended because the security of using KDFs as stream cipher algorithms has not been sufficiently investigated.
contents.html_ja: 導出鍵素材の長さ \(L\) は、KDF出力を利用する暗号アルゴリズムの要件によって決まる。暗号鍵の長さは、その鍵を使用するアルゴリズム（例：ブロック暗号またはメッセージ認証コード）と、求めるセキュリティ強度によって決まる。利用側アプリケーションが課す制限がない場合、必要な長さを持つ導出鍵素材の任意の区間を鍵として指定できる。ただし、導出鍵素材から複数の鍵（または初期化ベクトルなど他種のパラメータ）を得る場合、それらはKDF出力の互いに重ならない区間から選ばなければならない。したがって、\(L\) の値は、導出鍵素材から得る鍵およびその他のパラメータの長さの合計以上でなければならない。区間を公開パラメータ（公開IVなど）として使用する場合、KDF出力を解析するときに混乱が生じないよう注意が必要である。プロトコル層の攻撃により、一方の当事者がKDF出力の秘密部分を誤って開示するよう仕向けられる可能性がある。導出鍵素材を用いるプロトコルのセキュリティは、本勧告の対象外である。導出鍵素材を鍵ストリーム（ストリーム暗号など）として使用することは推奨されない。KDFをストリーム暗号アルゴリズムとして用いる安全性が十分に調査されていないためである。

contents.html: Input Data Encoding
contents.html_ja: 入力データの符号化

contents.html: The input data of a key-derivation function consists of different data fields (e.g., a \(\mathit{Label}\), the \(\mathit{Context}\), and the length of the output keying material). In Section 4, each of the data fields that represents certain information is encoded as a bit string. The encoding method shall define a one-to-one mapping from the set of all possible input information for that data field to a set of corresponding bit strings. The different data fields shall be assembled in a specific order. The encoding method (including the field order) may be defined in a larger context (e.g., by the protocol that uses a key-derivation function). The encoding method shall be designed for unambiguous conversion of the combined input information to a unique bit string. Unambiguous encoding for input data is required to deter attacks on the KDF that depend on manipulating the input data. For detailed discussions of such attacks, see [10].

contents.html: Key Separation
contents.html_ja: 鍵の分離

contents.html: In this Recommendation, key separation is a security requirement for the cryptographic keys derived from the same key-derivation key. The keys shall be separate in the sense that the compromise of some keys will not degrade the security strength of any of the other keys. In the families of KDFs specified in this Recommendation, key separation can be achieved through different approaches for the following two situations.
contents.html_ja: 本勧告では、同じ鍵導出鍵から導出される暗号鍵について、鍵分離をセキュリティ要件とする。鍵の一部が侵害されても、他の鍵のセキュリティ強度が低下しないという意味で、鍵は分離されなければならない。本勧告に規定するKDF族では、次の二つの状況に対して異なる方法で鍵分離を実現できる。

contents.html: When keying material for multiple cryptographic keys is obtained from the output of a single execution of a key-derivation function, the segments of the keying material used for the different keys need to be cryptographically separate: the compromise of some of the keys must not degrade the security of any of the other keys that are obtained from the output of the same execution of a KDF. That is, the compromise of some of the keys must not make the task of distinguishing any of the other keys from random strings with the same length easier than the task would be if none of the keys were compromised. In order to satisfy this requirement when using the key-derivation functions specified in this Recommendation, different keys shall be obtained from disjointed (i.e., non-overlapping) segments of the derived keying material.
contents.html_ja: 1回の鍵導出関数実行の出力から複数の暗号鍵用の鍵素材を得る場合、各鍵に用いる鍵素材の区間は暗号学的に分離されている必要がある。一部の鍵が侵害されても、同じKDF実行の出力から得られた他の鍵のセキュリティが低下してはならない。すなわち、一部の鍵が侵害されても、他の鍵を同じ長さのランダム文字列から識別する作業が、どの鍵も侵害されていない場合より容易になってはならない。本勧告に規定する鍵導出関数を用いてこの要件を満たすには、異なる鍵を導出鍵素材の互いに重ならない区間から得なければならない。

contents.html: 2. When keying material for multiple cryptographic keys is obtained from the output of multiple executions of a particular key-derivation function using the same value for \(K_{\mathit{IN}}\), the keying materials output by different calls to the KDF need to be cryptographically separate: the compromise of the keying material output from one of the executions of the KDF must not degrade the security of any of the keying material output from the other executions of the KDF using the same \(K_{\mathit{IN}}\). That is, the compromise must not make the task of predicting (or determining) the value of any of the other keying material easier than if none of the keying material were compromised. contents.html: Context Binding
contents.html_ja: コンテキストの結び付け

contents.html: Derived keying material should be bound to all relying entities and other information to identify the derived keying material. This is called context binding. In particular, the identity (or identifier, as the term is defined in [2] and [3]) of each entity that will access (i.e., derive, hold, use, and/or distribute) any segment of the keying material should be included in the Context string input to the KDF, provided that this information is known by each entity who derives the keying material. In addition to identities, other information related to the derived keying material (e.g., session identifiers, sequence numbers) as well as a nonce may be included in the Context string, assuming that the information can be communicated (e.g., by means of the relying protocol).

column_reflow.proof_note: This paragraph (Derived keying material should be bound...) is printed on page 24, not page 25; it duplicates page 24 block 1 and does not belong on this page

contents.html: Context binding may not necessarily increase the security strength of an application that makes use of a derived key. However, the binding may provide a way to detect protocol errors by providing assurance that all parties who (correctly) derive the keying material share the same understanding of who will access it and in which session it will be used. If those parties have different understandings, then they will derive different keying material. When that keying material is used in a protocol, the protocol will likely fail to complete its execution and, therefore, will indicate errors to the participants.
Key Control Security
contents.html_ja: 鍵制御に対する安全性

contents.html: When multiple parties contribute to the input of a key-derivation process, key-control security (or key-control resistance) is attained when the parties have assurance that (even with knowledge of the input key \(K_{\mathit{IN}}\)) no single party (or proper subset of the contributors) can manipulate the process in such a way as to force output keying material to a preselected value (regardless of the contributions of the others) to the detriment of any applications relying on that keying material. When CMAC is used as the PRF and multiple blocks of input data are involved, there are scenarios in which an entity that knows \(K_{\mathit{IN}}\) and has sufficient freedom of choice in its contribution to the KDF input (after all other inputs are known) may be able to unduly influence the output keying material. See Appendix B for an example. If key control security is a desired property, then HMAC or KMAC should be used as PRFs for key derivation unless, for example, AES is the only primitive implemented in the platform or using CMAC has a resource benefit. If CMAC is used as the PRF in a key-derivation function, then to achieve key control security, the input to the PRF needs to be specified in such a way that a single party cannot flexibly select any significant portion of the input data. Some methods are suggested in Section 4.1, 4.2, and 4.3 to mitigate key-control issues.

contents.html: Appendix D. Glossary

approved — An algorithm or technique for a specific cryptographic use that is specified in a FIPS or NIST Recommendation, adopted in a FIPS or NIST Recommendation, or specified in a list of NIST-approved security functions.

cryptographic key — A bit string used as a secret parameter by a cryptographic algorithm. In this Recommendation, a cryptographic key is either a random bit string of a length specified by the cryptographic algorithm or a pseudorandom bit string of the required length that is computationally indistinguishable from one selected uniformly at random from the set of all bit strings of that length.
entity — An individual (person), organization, device, or a combination thereof. In this Recommendation, an entity may be a functional unit that executes certain processes.
hash function — A function that maps a bit string of arbitrary length to a fixed-length bit string. Approved hash functions satisfy the following properties:
(Collision resistance) It is computationally infeasible to find any two distinct inputs that map to the same output.
(Preimage resistance) Given a randomly chosen target output, it is computationally infeasible to find any input that maps to that output. (This property is called the one-way property.)
(Second preimage resistance) Given one input value, it is computationally infeasible to find a second (distinct) input value that maps to the same output as the first value.
This Recommendation uses the strength of the preimage resistance of a hash function as a contributing factor when determining the security strength provided by a key-derivation function.

key derivation — The process by which keying material is derived from 1) either a cryptographic key or a shared secret produced during a key-agreement scheme and 2) other data. This Recommendation specifies key derivation from an existing cryptographic key and other data.
key-derivation function (KDF) — A function that, with the input of a cryptographic key and other data, generates a bit string called the keying material, as defined in this Recommendation.
key-derivation key (KDK) — A key used as an input to a key-derivation function to derive additional keying material.
key establishment — A procedure conducted by two or more participants, after which the resultant keying material is shared by all participants.
key hierarchy — A multiple-level tree structure such that each node represents a key and each branch – pointing from one node to another – indicates a key derivation from one key to another key.
keying material — A bit string such that non-overlapping segments of the string (with the required lengths) can be used as cryptographic keys or other secret (pseudorandom) parameters.

message authentication code (MAC) — A family of secret-key cryptographic algorithms acting on input data of arbitrary length to produce an output value of a specified length (called the MAC of the input data). The MAC can be employed to provide an authentication of the origin of data and/or data-integrity protection. In this Recommendation, approved MAC algorithms are used to determine families of pseudorandom functions (indexed by the choice of key) that are employed during key derivation.
mode of iteration A method for iterating the multiple invocations of a pseudorandom function in order to derive the keying material with a required length.

original_blocks.html: It is recommended that the length of a KDK used by a KDF be at least as large as the targeted security strength (in bits) of any application that will be supported by the use of the derived keying material. This may affect the choice of the MAC algorithm used to implement a PRF-based key-derivation function, since the possibilities for the KDK size are determined by what is allowed for the MAC keys. For example, when using CMAC as a PRF, the key length is uniquely determined by the underlying block cipher. In this case, an implementation should check whether the key-derivation key length is consistent with the length required by the PRF. However, some PRFs can accommodate different key lengths. If HMAC is used as the PRF, then a KDF can use a key-derivation key of essentially any length. It is worth noting, however, that if the chosen key is longer than one input block for the hash function underlying HMAC, that key will be hashed, and the (much shorter) h-bit output will be used as the HMAC key instead. In this case, given a pair consisting of the input data (other than the key) and enough corresponding output of the KDF, the hashed key can likely be recovered in (at most) 2h computations of the KDF. Therefore, the security strength of an HMAC-based key-derivation function may be decreased by increasing the length of the KDK beyond the length of an input block of the underlying hash function.

original_blocks.html: The length of the derived keying material L depends on the requirements of the cryptographic algorithms that rely on the KDF output. The length of a given cryptographic key is determined by the algorithm that will employ it (e.g., a block cipher or a message authentication code) and the desired security strength. In the absence of limitations that may be imposed by relying applications, any segment of the derived keying material that has the required length can be specified for use as a key, subject to the following restriction: when multiple keys (or any other types of parameters, such as initialization vectors) are obtained from the derived keying material, they shall be selected from disjointed (i.e., non-overlapping) segments of the KDF output. Therefore, the value of L shall be greater than or equal to the sum of the lengths of the keys and other types of parameters that will be obtained from the derived keying material. Care must be taken to avoid confusion when parsing KDF output if any segments are used as public parameters (such as public IVs). Attacks on the protocol level may attempt to cause one party to mistakenly release a secret portion of the KDF output. The security of any protocol using the derived keying material is beyond the scope of this Recommendation. The use of the derived keying material as a key stream (as in a stream cipher) is not recommended because the security of using KDFs as stream cipher algorithms has not been sufficiently investigated.

original_blocks.html: The input data of a key-derivation function consists of different data fields (e.g., a Label, the Context, and the length of the output keying material). In Section 4, each of the data fields that represents certain information is encoded as a bit string. The encoding method shall define a one-to-one mapping from the set of all possible input information for that data field to a set of corresponding bit strings. The different data fields shall be assembled in a specific order. The encoding method (including the field order) may be defined in a larger context (e.g., by the protocol that uses a key-derivation function). rebuilt_blocks.html: When a party obtains a cryptographic key, additional keys will often be needed. There are numerous methods for obtaining the keying material required by approved cryptographic algorithms (see SP 800-133, Rev. 2 [1] for a discussion of the recommended techniques). The requisite keying material is often obtained from the output of a key-derivation function (KDF) that takes a preexisting cryptographic key (and other data) as input. Key-derivation functions are used to derive additional keys from a cryptographic key. The key-derivation functions specified in the original edition (2008) of NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-1081 used HMAC and CMAC as pseudorandom functions. In Revision 1, a KDF using KMAC is added in Section 4.4.

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note that the key-derivation methods employed as components of key-agreement schemes (as described in [2], [3], and [5]) include two-step methods in which the first step consists of extracting a KDK from a shared secret precursor. These extracted KDKs are not part of the output of a key-agreement scheme. They are only used to derive output keying material during a single execution of a scheme and then destroyed (along with all other sensitive, locally stored data associated with that particular execution). In keeping with the usual terminology, the output of a key-derivation function is called the derived keying material and may subsequently be segmented into multiple keys. Any disjoint segments of the derived keying material (with the required lengths) can be used as cryptographic keys for the intended algorithms. Two different key-establishment scenarios may use the KDF: one in which multiple parties share the same key-derivation key and are able to separately derive the same keying material, and the other in which one entity derives keying material using a key-derivation key known only to itself and distributes the derived keying material to other entities. When multiple parties share the same key-derivation key, the cryptographic application employing a KDF must define the way to convert (i.e., parse) the keying material into different keys. For example, when 256 bits of keying material are derived, the application may specify that the first 128 bits will be used as a key for a message authentication code and that the second 128 bits will be used as an encryption key for a given encryption algorithm. In the case where a single party derives the keying material, a re-derivation can produce the same keys (when required).
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: なお、鍵合意方式（[2]、[3]、[5]に記述）を構成する要素として用いられる鍵導出方法には、二段階方式が含まれる。この方式では、第1段階で共有秘密の前駆値からKDKを抽出する。抽出されたこれらのKDKは、鍵合意方式の出力の一部ではない。これらは、方式の1回の実行中に出力用の鍵素材を導出するためだけに使用され、その後（当該実行に関連する他のすべての機微なローカル保存データとともに）破棄される。通常の用語法に従い、鍵導出関数の出力を導出鍵素材と呼び、その後、複数の鍵に分割してもよい。導出鍵素材の互いに重ならない部分は、必要な長さを満たせば、対象アルゴリズムの暗号鍵として使用できる。KDFは、二つの異なる鍵確立シナリオで使用されることがある。一つは、複数の当事者が同じ鍵導出鍵を共有し、各自で同一の鍵素材を導出できる場合である。もう一つは、あるエンティティだけが知る鍵導出鍵を用いてそのエンティティが鍵素材を導出し、導出した鍵素材を他のエンティティに配布する場合である。複数の当事者が同じ鍵導出鍵を共有する場合、KDFを使用する暗号アプリケーションは、鍵素材を異なる鍵に変換（すなわち解析）する方法を定義しなければならない。例えば、256ビットの鍵素材を導出した場合、先頭の128ビットをメッセージ認証コードの鍵として使用し、次の128ビットを所定の暗号アルゴリズムの暗号化鍵として使用するよう、アプリケーションで指定できる。単一の当事者が鍵素材を導出する場合、必要に応じ、再導出によって同じ鍵を生成できる。

rebuilt_blocks.html: Derived keying material should be bound to all relying entities and other information to identify the derived keying material. This is called context binding. In particular, the identity (or identifier, as the term is defined in [2] and [3]) of each entity that will access (i.e., derive, hold, use, and/or distribute) any segment of the keying material should be included in the Context string input to the KDF, provided that this information is known by each entity who derives the keying material. In addition to identities, other information related to the derived keying material (e.g., session identifiers, sequence numbers) as well as a nonce may be included in the Context string, assuming that the information can be communicated (e.g., by means of the relying protocol). Context binding may not necessarily increase the security strength of an application that makes use of a derived key. However, the binding may provide a way to detect protocol errors by providing assurance that all parties who (correctly) derive the keying material share the same understanding of who will access it and in which session it will be used. If those parties have different understandings, then they will derive different keying material. When that keying material is used in a protocol, the protocol will likely fail to complete its execution and, therefore, will indicate errors to the participants.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 導出鍵素材は、それを使用するすべてのエンティティおよび導出鍵素材を識別するその他の情報に結び付けるべきである。これをコンテキストの結び付けと呼ぶ。特に、鍵素材の任意の区間にアクセスする（すなわち導出、保持、使用、および／または配布する）各エンティティの識別情報（または[2]および[3]で定義する識別子）を、KDFへのContext文字列入力に含めるべきである。ただし、その情報を鍵素材の導出者全員が知っていることを条件とする。識別情報に加えて、導出鍵素材に関連するその他の情報（例：セッション識別子、シーケンス番号）やノンスも、伝達可能である（例：依存プロトコルを介して伝達できる）ことを前提にContext文字列に含めてもよい。コンテキストの結び付けによって、導出鍵を使用するアプリケーションのセキュリティ強度が必ず高まるとは限らない。しかし、結び付けにより、（正しく）鍵素材を導出するすべての当事者が、誰がどのセッションで鍵素材にアクセスするかについて同じ理解を共有していることを確認でき、プロトコルエラーを検出できる場合がある。当事者間で理解が異なれば、異なる鍵素材が導出される。その鍵素材をプロトコルで使用すると、実行が完了せず、参加者にエラーが通知される可能性が高い。

rebuilt_blocks.html: key derivation The process by which keying material is derived from 1) either a cryptographic key or a shared secret produced during a key-agreement scheme and 2) other data. This Recommendation specifies key derivation from an existing cryptographic key and other data.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 鍵導出（key derivation） 1) 暗号鍵または鍵共有方式で生成された共有秘密と、2) その他のデータから鍵材料を導出するプロセス。本勧告では、既存の暗号鍵とその他のデータからの鍵導出を規定する。

rebuilt_blocks.html: key-derivation function (KDF) A function that, with the input of a cryptographic key and other data, generates a bit string called the keying material, as defined in this Recommendation.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 鍵導出関数（KDF） 暗号鍵とその他のデータを入力として受け取り、本勧告で定義する鍵材料と呼ばれるビット列を生成する関数。

rebuilt_blocks.html: key-derivation key (KDK) A key used as an input to a key-derivation function to derive additional keying material.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 鍵導出鍵（KDK） 追加の鍵材料を導出するために、鍵導出関数への入力として使用する鍵。

rebuilt_blocks.html: key establishment A procedure conducted by two or more participants, after which the resultant keying material is shared by all participants.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 鍵確立（key establishment） 2人以上の参加者が実施する手順であり、手順の完了後、生成された鍵材料をすべての参加者で共有する。

rebuilt_blocks.html: key hierarchy A multiple-level tree structure such that each node represents a key and each branch – pointing from one node to another – indicates a key derivation from one key to another key.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 鍵階層（key hierarchy） 各ノードが鍵を表す多段の木構造。あるノードから別のノードへ向かう各枝は、ある鍵から別の鍵への鍵導出を示す。

rebuilt_blocks.html: keying material A bit string such that non-overlapping segments of the string (with the required lengths) can be used as cryptographic keys or other secret (pseudorandom) parameters.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 鍵材料（keying material） 必要な長さを持つ互いに重ならない部分列を、暗号鍵またはその他の秘密の（疑似ランダムな）パラメータとして使用できるビット列。

rebuilt_blocks.html: message authentication code (MAC) A family of secret-key cryptographic algorithms acting on input data of arbitrary length to produce an output value of a specified length (called the MAC of the input data). The MAC can be employed to provide an authentication of the origin of data and/or data-integrity protection. In this Recommendation, approved MAC algorithms are used to determine families of pseudorandom functions (indexed by the choice of key) that are employed during key derivation.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: メッセージ認証コード（MAC） 任意長の入力データを処理し、MACと呼ばれる指定長の出力値を生成する、秘密鍵暗号アルゴリズムの一群。MACは、データの出所の認証および／またはデータ完全性の保護に利用できる。本勧告では、鍵導出時に用いる疑似ランダム関数の一群（鍵の選択によってインデックス付けされる）を定めるため、承認済みMACアルゴリズムを使用する。
